rules.sentence: Although vertebral osteomyelitis is typically caused by a single pathogen, such as Staphylococcus aureus or Propionibacterium acnes, back pain is the most common symptom, while fever is often absent.
Neurological impairment occurs in approximately one-third of patients with vertebral osteomyelitis.
Common risk factors include advanced age, immunosuppression, diabetes, intravenous (IV) drug use, and malnutrition.
Apply appropriate diagnostic modalities, including blood cultures, imaging studies, and biopsies, to confirm vertebral osteomyelitis in patients with suspected infection.
Implement evidence-based management strategies, including pathogen-targeted antibiotic therapy, to optimize treatment outcomes for vertebral osteomyelitis patients.
